title: Canadian Poplar: Old Poplars You Can Visit
meta_description: The Netherlands' oldest poplar is a hybrid bred for timber and never meant to last. Four Canadian poplars mapped, in four countries.
intro: The oldest poplar in the Netherlands grows behind a concert hall in Arnhem, on the last stretch of moat the city never filled in, and it is not supposed to have got this far. Canadian poplar is a hybrid of Europe's black poplar and an American cottonwood, bred for timber and shelter belts, fast, soft and finished within decades rather than centuries. Arnhem's has stood since somewhere between 1750 and 1800. The other three are dated in decades, and what makes them worth the walk is what happened around them. Warsaw's was already mature when the ground it stands on became a transit camp in 1944. Den Bosch's went in around 1941, under occupation, and was a young tree when the fighting reached the city. Antwerp's is simply enormous, 35 metres with six metres of clear trunk before the crown starts.
